like: verb
enjoy something or think it is nice or good
typical: like + noun/-ing: like music, like swimming. NOT for: wanting (see would like).
I like hot tea in the morning.
Do you like your new job?
verb
think a person is nice or have a friendly feeling towards them
typical: like + person. NOT for: romantic love.
I really like your sister.
He doesn't like his boss.
verb
do something regularly or by preference
typical: like to + verb. NOT for: a single wish.
I like to get up early.
She likes to read before bed.
verb
(would like) want something, or politely offer or ask
typical: would like + noun/to + verb. NOT for: general enjoyment.
I would like a coffee, please.
Would you like to come with us?
preposition
similar to, or in the same way as
typical: look/sound/taste/feel like + noun. NOT for: enjoyment.
He looks like his father.
It tastes like chicken.
preposition
for example, such as
typical: noun + like + examples. NOT for: comparison of two things.
I enjoy sports like tennis and swimming.
She loves fruit like mangoes and pineapples.
last: adjective
coming at the end, after all others
typical: the last bus/day/page/one. NOT for: most recent.
This is the last bus.
She was the last to arrive.
adjective
most recent, just before now
typical: last week/year/night/time. NOT for: final in a series.
I saw him last week.
What did you do last night?
adverb
most recently, or at the end after everyone else
typical: when I last saw her, came last, last of all. NOT for: duration.
When did you last see him?
He finished last in the race.
verb
continue for a period of time
typical: last + time expression. NOT for: final position.
The meeting lasted two hours.
The film lasts almost three hours.
verb
continue in good condition, or be enough for a time
typical: won't last, last for + time. NOT for: events.
This good weather won't last.
Our supplies will last a week.
leave: verb
go away from a place or person
typical: leave + place, leave for + place, leave at + time. NOT for: stopping a job (see next sense).
We leave at eight.
She left the office early.
verb
let something stay where it is, often by accident
typical: leave + object + place/adjective. NOT for: departure.
I left my keys at home.
Leave the door open.
verb
stop working at a job or going to a school or organization
typical: leave school/work/a job/the army. NOT for: temporary absence.
He left school at sixteen.
She left her job last month.
verb
end a relationship and go away from your partner
typical: leave + husband/wife/partner. NOT for: leaving a place.
Martha left her husband last year.
He never believed she would leave him.
verb
remain after the rest has been used or taken
typical: be left, there is/are + noun + left. NOT for: departure.
There are only two days left.
Is there any milk left?
verb
deliver or put a message for someone
typical: leave a message/note for sb. NOT for: departure.
Can I leave a message for Anna?
She left a note on the table.
verb
let someone else decide or deal with something
typical: leave it to sb, leave sb to do sth. NOT for: departure.
I'll leave it to you to decide.
Leave the cooking to me.
verb
delay doing something until later
typical: leave sth until later/tomorrow/the last minute. NOT for: forgetting objects.
Don't leave your homework until the last minute.
Let's leave this for today.
look: verb
direct your eyes towards something to see it
typical: look at/out of/up/down. NOT for: seeming.
Look at this picture.
He looked out of the window.
verb
seem or appear
typical: look + adjective, look like + noun. NOT for: using your eyes on purpose.
You look tired.
The house looks old.
verb
try to find something
typical: look for + thing. NOT for: just seeing.
I'm looking for my keys.
She is looking for a new flat.
verb
consider or examine something carefully
typical: look at the problem/situation/idea. NOT for: physical looking.
We need to look at all the options.
Let's look at the budget again.
noun
an act of looking at something
typical: have/take a look (at sth). NOT for: appearance.
Take a look at this photo.
Can I have a quick look at your notes?
noun
(looks) the way someone or something appears
typical: good looks, by the looks of it. NOT for: an act of looking.
He has his father's good looks.
By the looks of it, it will rain.
